description: PM Projects page — PM's project list (search/sort/pagination/summary bar, active vs completed/archived split) and per-project developer list (search/sort/filter, no pagination, per-developer allocation/leave/notice-period fields), plus per-developer Update Allocation entry points into the ALCTKT ticketing workflow.
edgeCases: PM with zero currently-managed projects — project list shows an empty state, summary bar shows 0 active projects.

A project whose PM was reassigned via the nightly Zoho sync — the previous PM should stop seeing it (up to 24-hour sync lag is acceptable per source) and the new PM should inherit visibility, including all existing tickets for that project.
A project with Project.projectManagerId left null because its Zoho projectManagerEmail did not match any Employee.email — verify it does not incorrectly appear on any PM's project list.
Developer list for a project with zero currently-allocated developers — empty-state message shown; no pagination controls rendered (developer list is never paginated).
A developer who is both serving a notice period AND has an active/upcoming leave — both indicators shown together without one overwriting the other.

Dynamic-allocation developer row — the allocation-percentage field renders disabled/read-only rather than simply hidden, and the dynamic allocation expectation note (1–2 hrs/day or 10–20 hrs/month) is visible.
Project list pagination boundary — exactly 100, 200, or 300 projects, and one more than each threshold, to verify the correct page-size behaviour and page-count computation.
Sort by 'last updated date' with two or more projects sharing the identical timestamp — verify stable secondary ordering.
Search project name / developer name with special characters, apostrophes, accents, or Unicode — correct matching without crashing.

'Hours logged on this project' displayed from Zoho Analytics is stale/out of date relative to a very recent time entry — verify the UI clearly reflects the data's Zoho-sourced nature rather than implying real-time accuracy.
Developer list filter combining Leave status AND Notice period simultaneously — verify both filters apply together (AND, not OR).

A project that transitions from Active to Completed/Archived status mid-session (or between page loads) — verify it moves from the Active section to the Completed/Archived section without a manual-refresh discrepancy.
Dual-role user (PM + RM/TM/EM) opening the PM Projects page — must see PM-scoped data only (their managed projects), with the paired org role having no bearing on this page.
Navigate the project list across all available page sizes (100/200/300) and verify no project is duplicated or dropped between pages (regression-derived, pagination risk).
Sort the project list and developer list by each sortable column, including datasets with duplicate values in the sorted column, and verify stable ordering (regression-derived, sorting risk).

Apply developer-list filters (leave status, notice period) individually and combined, including a combination matching zero developers, and verify the empty-state message is shown (regression-derived, filtering risk).

After a Dynamic Update Allocation ticket is approved (ProjectAssignment archived/soft-deleted), verify the developer no longer appears in that project's developer list without requiring a manual page refresh (regression-derived, archived-record-visibility risk).

Use a session without PM or PMO role (plain RM/TM/EM/Employee) to attempt loading the PM Projects page/route directly via URL, and verify access is denied at both UI and API levels (regression-derived, role-based-access risk).
Allocation start date exactly 2 calendar months before today (e.g. today 2026-09-28, start 2026-07-28) — must NOT be flagged Long-Running ('more than 2 months'); live dev agrees.
Allocation start date 2 calendar months + 1 day before today — must be flagged Long-Running.
Allocation 60 or 61 days old but less than 2 calendar months — shows whether the rule is days-based or month-based (live: not flagged, so month-based).
Month-end arithmetic: today = 31 Mar / 30 Apr / 29 Feb — 'two months ago' resolves to a date that does not exist (31 Jan, 29/30/31 Dec); confirm deterministic behaviour.
Long-running allocation whose end date is in the past (ended) — must not be flagged Long-Running nor counted on the card.
Long-running allocation whose end date is today — still running today; confirm it stays flagged and also appears under Upcoming Deallocation.
Open-ended allocation (end date null) older than 2 months — must be flagged.
Allocation with a percentage/type change via Update Allocation ticket (new SCHEDULED timeline segment) — Long-Running age must count from the original start date (continuity preserved).
Allocation that was deallocated and re-allocated to the same project with a gap — 'continuously' rule: age must reset at the re-allocation start date.
Back-to-back re-allocation with no gap (end D, new start D+1) — decide whether this is continuous (should probably stay Long-Running).

Employee with multiple allocations on different projects, only some older than 2 months — only those allocations carry the LR label; the employee matches the Long Running filter once (no duplicate rows).
Employee with two allocations on the same project (e.g. FIXED + DYNAMIC) — each evaluated separately; card count counts allocations, not employees.
Start date = today — not Upcoming (already active), counts as Recent (started within 30 days).
Start date = tomorrow — Upcoming; must not appear in the active allocations table on Project Detail.
Start date exactly 30 days ago — boundary of Recent window (inclusive?); 31 days ago — must not be Recent unless end date is within window.
End date exactly 30 days ago / 31 days ago — Recent boundary via end date.
End date exactly today+30 / today+31 — Upcoming Deallocation boundary.
Far-future upcoming allocation (e.g. start 2027-09-01) — listed under Upcoming, not counted as Recent.
Allocation of an exited/soft-deleted employee (deletedAt set) — must not be flagged Long-Running or counted in the card (live dev: counted — candidate defect).
Project where every allocation is long-running vs a project with none — card filter must include the former and exclude the latter.
Upcoming section with 0 upcoming allocations — requirement implies a section; build hides it entirely (returns null). Confirm expected behaviour.
Combining the Allocation filter with other filters (Department, Projects, Leave & Status) and with search — AND semantics, chip shown per filter.
Selecting multiple Allocation options at once (checkbox group) — union (OR) semantics expected; confirm.
Allocation filter that matches zero records — readable empty state (e.g. 'No projects found' / 'No data available'), never a bare dash.
Timezone: user in a non-IST timezone near midnight — flag computed server-side with date-only values must not flip by a day in the UI.
Changing the time-range selector ('Last 15 days' / 30d / 3m) must not change the Long-Running flag or card count (flag depends on today, not the logged-hours window).
businessRules: Pagination controls on the PM Projects project list must correctly reflect the total record count; navigating between the 100/200/300 page-size pages must not duplicate or drop projects.

Sorting the project list by project name or last updated date, and the developer list by developer name/allocation %/start date, must produce a stable order; re-sorting by the same column must toggle direction consistently, including when records share identical values in the sorted column.

Applying developer-list filters (leave status, notice period) must update the displayed developers accordingly; clearing filters must restore the full unfiltered developer list, and a filter combination matching zero developers must show an explicit empty-state rather than a blank/stale list.

Once a Dynamic-allocation Update Allocation ticket is approved and the ProjectAssignment is archived (soft-deleted), the corresponding developer must no longer appear in that project's developer list.

Each role's PM Projects page access must be enforced at both UI and API levels: PM sees only their managed projects, PMO sees all projects, and an org-only role (RM/TM/EM) without a paired PM role must have no access to the page at all.

The Long-Running Allocations card count, the number of LR badges across the user's projects, and pm-projects/stats longRunningAllocationCount must be equal at all times (employee/allocation count consistency).

Applying an Allocation filter must update both the displayed rows and the result count ('Showing x - y of N results'); clearing it must restore the full list; a zero-match filter must show a readable empty state, and an active filter must always be visible as a chip.
Allocation-stage data (LR/Upcoming flags, stats count, Allocation filter) must be enforced per role at UI (hidden/Access Denied) and API (403) level; Employee persona sees none.
After an allocation is deallocated (or an employee exits), the LR flag and card count must update without a manual refresh, and the allocation must not stay counted.
Hovering the Availability 'i' icon and LR badges must show the same tooltip content on every row with that data, including the last row and rows on page 2.
